title: Legacy CRM Release Test Strategy — Seven-Phase Methodology
summary: A seven-phase release testing methodology for a legacy life sciences CRM platform, covering packaging through go-live with backward compatibility validation, regression testing tiers, and multi-team coordination across six global locations.

findings.seven_phases: Phase 1: Packaging (build assembly and initial verification). Phase 2: Transparency Testing (automated quality assurance followed by manual quality assurance, validating backward compatibility). Phase 3: Regression (structured test execution across priority tiers). Phase 4a: UAT Production Smoke (quick validation of production readiness). Phase 4b: UAT (full user acceptance testing). Phase 5: Localization and Pre-Production (language validation and production environment preparation). Phase 6: Client Sandbox (customer-specific sandbox testing with production data). Phase 7: Go-Live (production deployment and verification).
findings.backward_compatibility_matrix: Five test cases covering upgrade permutations: Case 0 (clean install with current versions of all components), Case 1 (previous platform version, previous metadata service, current app), Case 2 (current platform, previous metadata service, current app), Case 3 (previous platform, current metadata service, current app), Case 4 (current platform, current metadata service, previous app). Additional packages for region-specific deployments are tested in combination with each case.
findings.test_priority_methodology: Critical and High priority test cases: all MAT (Minimum Acceptance Testing), CORE (core functionality), and AUX (auxiliary) scenarios executed across all backward compatibility cases. Medium priority: MAT scenarios executed through the last six major releases plus all scenarios for the current release. Low priority: MAT scenarios only. This risk-based approach concentrates testing effort on the highest-impact areas.
findings.test_types: Functional tests (feature behavior validation), Compliance tests (tagged for quality score tracking and GxP relevance), Orchestration tests (cross-product integration covering four product combinations), and Security tests (applied when security-relevant changes are present).
findings.team_distribution: Eight testing teams across six global locations providing time-zone coverage for continuous testing execution. Teams are organized by functional area and backward compatibility case assignment.
findings.timeline_pattern: Approximately 12 weeks from packaging start to production go-live. Transparency testing overlaps with early regression. UAT runs in parallel with localization and pre-production validation. Client sandbox testing provides the final pre-production gate.
